### What does this PR do?

Extend the native VeOmni LoRA integration to M3.1-Flash multimodal experts and export temporary merged full weights for vLLM synchronization. Dense, shared-expert and independent-expert merges preserve actor/optimizer parameter storage.

The target checkpoint is **MiniMax-M3.1-Flash**. Its checkpoint config uses `model_type="minimax_m3_vl"` and architecture `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`; existing `minimax_m3` module/class identifiers are retained for compatibility. They are architecture identifiers, not a claim that a different model version was validated.

Default targets cover text attention and MLP/experts, excluding vision, lm_head and the no_grad sparse indexer. Explicit dense/vision/projector targets remain supported; explicit indexer targets fail. The generic Qwen3 EP1/SP1 restrictions remain unchanged.

**Stacked draft:** current main `2ab35292039a51175a4b3d3b3b2d76e951a0d3e4` has been merged at `7ae23d53769a3b1078b151183cfd2a70b11c8ccc`. The branch includes generic dense-LoRA #8307 at `8f42981f4c3f2d1e8723e78f6842e3d38198b563`, the full-parameter export proposed in #8417, and the companion VeOmni source below. Dependency ancestry is retained for attribution; the overall diff includes inherited scaffolding. The three engine conflicts are resolved by merging adapters in the unquantized HF exporter, keeping checkpoint output separate from the optional rollout quantizer. Current vLLM admission handling is preserved. GitHub reports no merge conflicts against that main revision; dependency selection/locking and native acceptance remain pending.

### Why this is not duplicate work

Searched open [VeOmni LoRA](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+VeOmni+LoRA) and [MiniMax](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+MiniMax) PRs on 2026-10-28. #8307 provides Qwen3 Dense native LoRA and excludes expert adapters; it is a dependency. #8353 is the verl-native FSDP2 text-model route. This draft supplies the VeOmni multimodal expert-LoRA/export path, building on #8417.

### Test

- **50 CPU cases passed** on the reviewed snapshot: 30 inherited full-weight/image/export cases and 20 target-selection, CPU/meta dtype, dense/shared/independent merge and public-export regressions.
- After the current-main merge, **55 CPU cases passed (5.73s)**: the original 50 plus five engine export-routing cases. The added tests execute the actual engine methods with isolated backend imports, covering M3.1-Flash and Qwen3 LoRA with quantization enabled/disabled and the non-LoRA converter path. The checkpoint callback exports floating weights, while rollout applies the configured quantizer after adapter merging.
- A deliberate incorrect-merge control that omits rollout quantization triggers 3 failures / 2 passes in the new five-case suite; the corrected implementation passes. This control is a simulated integration regression, not a claim that unchanged upstream was tested with the entire suite.
- Four frozen-bias regressions fail on the prior implementation (46 passed / 4 failed) and pass with the reviewed correction (50 passed). They cover public bias names/values and nonmutating FP32/BF16 export for explicit vision/projector targets.
- Export tests use small native-accessor substitutes, not the complete distributed model.
- Scoped Ruff lint/format and launch-template bash syntax pass.
- Current-main update: pinned Ruff 0.13.1 lint and format checks pass for all 14 Python files in the changed-source snapshot; both launch scripts pass `bash -n`.
- Command: `python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts= -q tests`, with plugin autoload disabled, in an isolated task-owned source snapshot using existing Python 3.12 server packages.
- The inherited generic dense-LoRA suite, standard conftest/scheduler, complete combined model startup, accelerator kernels, FSDP2 materialization, checkpoint resume and full-repository pre-commit have not been accepted on this final published combination.

### Historical full-model evidence

The experimental LoRA stack used the full **60-layer / 128-expert M3.1-Flash**, rank/alpha 64, training EP4/SP4 and rollout TP32/EP1, with DSpark3 enabled. Two actor updates completed; correct sampled responses were 90/128 and 94/128, with finite gradient norms 0.02171357 and 0.01769571. Greedy accuracy changed from 10/16 to 15/16 on the same 16 examples used for training. Step 3 later stalled and was stopped; no checkpoint was produced.

These are historical overfit/debug results from the experimental stack, not new validation of this extracted branch, a held-out evaluation, long-run stability, or SFT evidence.

### Dependency / precision contract

Companion upstream PR: [VeOmni #1380](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/1380).

Companion source is public at [Li-Jicheng/VeOmni@`d51ffd7ca60b65be361091c2f3c95828772262ef`](https://github.com/Li-Jicheng/VeOmni/commit/d51ffd7ca60b65be361091c2f3c95828772262ef). It combines VeOmni #1315, the pinned #1337 dense-reference context, and expert LoRA.

```bash
uv pip install --no-deps 'veomni @ git+https://github.com/Li-Jicheng/VeOmni.git@d51ffd7ca60b65be361091c2f3c95828772262ef'
```

This overrides the source only in an already compatible environment. The inherited #8307 pyproject/uv.lock pin still points to its own dependency revision, not this combined source: **final dependency pin replacement and uv lock regeneration/validation remain required before merge**. The public integration SHA is not a release.

Frozen base storage remains BF16; trainable/router storage and score-correction bias stay FP32. This does not establish FP32 router execution. Temporary adapter merges use FP32 and export in the base dtype, without modifying live parameters. Native disable_adapter supplies the reference; updated base parameters are not restored by disabling adapters.

### Checklist before submission / requesting merge

- [x] Human reviewed every original changed line, understands the delta and attested relevant tests on 2026-10-28.
- [x] Exact companion VeOmni source published and linked.
- [x] Merge current main and resolve conflicts while preserving HF checkpoint / rollout quantization separation; submitting human reviewed the three-file update on 2026-10-28.
- [ ] Integrate eventual merged dependency revisions before marking ready for merge.
- [ ] Replace the inherited install pin and regenerate/validate uv.lock.
- [ ] Full repository pre-commit and combined native runtime tests.
- [ ] Accelerator/FSDP2/EP/checkpoint acceptance of the published stack.
- [ ] Maintainer CI request.

AI assistance was used for source adaptation, tests, review and PR preparation. The submitting user reviewed both the original delta and this current-main conflict resolution. The 55-case CPU run is attributed to the assistant; no new hardware or full-framework execution is claimed.

+MiniMax M3 with VeOmni and vLLM
+==============================
+
+This integration exports the unquantized ``minimax_m3_vl`` model from VeOmni's
+training layout into the public checkpoint layout consumed by vLLM. Dimensions
+and dense/MoE schedules come from the model config. It normalizes image
+placeholders before vLLM processor expansion and checks the expanded prompt.
+
+Dependencies
+------------
+
+The model and base SwiGLU-OAI operators currently require `VeOmni PR #1315
+<https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/1315>`_, inspected at
+``3fc30d7f306aa086e16859622b0369eab454f8df``. This is an unmerged source
+dependency, not a released PyPI version. The verl integration is based on
+``4d3ed12a7617c6b78ee0ac8f27dd7848bb0d11ee``. An exact combined VeOmni commit
+must be published and recorded before this integration can be installed with a
+frozen dependency lock; the existing default VeOmni pin is insufficient.
+
+Use a vLLM/vllm-ascend build with matching MiniMax M3 public-layout support.
+Record its commit, PyTorch, torch-npu and CANN versions as well as Python
+package versions. A conda package list alone does not identify editable source
+copies, import paths or native runtime libraries. No particular current
+vLLM/vllm-ascend pair is newly hardware-validated by this change.
+
+Usage
+-----
+
+``examples/grpo_trainer/run_minimax_m3_veomni.sh`` is an Ascend integration
+template. Supply ``MODEL_PATH``, ``TRAIN_FILES``, ``VAL_FILES``, ``NNODES``,
+``NPUS_PER_NODE``, ``TRAIN_EP``, ``TRAIN_SP``, ``ROLLOUT_TP`` and ``ROLLOUT_EP``
+for a prepared Ray cluster. The script uses full weight synchronization and
+eager rollout. Extra Hydra overrides are accepted at the end. It does not
+provision machines or install dependencies, and the new template has only been
+syntax-checked; size its batch and topology for the complete model.
+
+Validation boundaries
+---------------------
+
+CPU tests cover public tensor names/shapes, image tokens and two-process Gloo
+expert-row export. These tests need no model weights or accelerators. They do
+not establish NPU kernel behavior, full-model memory use or numerical training
+equivalence on the extracted source.
+
+Historical full-size M3.1-Flash evidence used 60 layers and 128 experts on
+16 machines/256 NPUs: training EP32/SP1 and rollout EP64, with DSpark disabled.
+It completed two actor updates and synchronizations. Rewards were 0.6476563
+and 0.7145833 on a shared 500-example training/evaluation set. The later driver
+exit was nonzero and there was no saved checkpoint. This is historical
+integration evidence, not a test of the new source or a long-run quality claim.
+
+Quantized checkpoints, MTP, adapter-only/delta synchronization and resumability
+are outside this full-parameter change. No SFT result is inferred from RL logs.
+
+
+Expert LoRA companion
+---------------------
+
+The expert-adapter extension additionally needs the generic native integration
+from `verl #8307 <https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8307>`_ (inspected at
+``8f42981f4c3f2d1e8723e78f6842e3d38198b563``), the native reference context from
+`VeOmni #1337 <https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/VeOmni/pull/1337>`_ (inspected at
+``3780b042594d8597b34e4fbc5e683de3aea2fac6``), and the companion SwiGLU-OAI
+expert-LoRA change. Publish a combined source commit and regenerate the lock
+before installation; none of these unmerged heads is an interchangeable release.
+
+Set ``actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=64``, ``lora_alpha=64``,
+``target_modules=all-linear`` and ``lora.merge=True``. For this model the default
+selects text attention and dense/shared MLP linears plus independent
+expert gate/up/down adapters; the frozen sparse indexer, vision and lm_head
+are excluded. Indexer targets are rejected because its projections run under
+no_grad without a published indexer training objective. Explicit dense
+target lists are preserved. For explicit vision/projector targets, original
+frozen dense biases are exported with their public names and unchanged values.
+Zero dropout, bias='none', FSDP2, mixed precision
+and a non-None parameter compute dtype are required. DDP/unsharded mixed-storage
+execution is rejected. Full merged weights are built in temporary storage and
+exported without mutating actor/optimizer weights. Reference inference uses the
+native disable_adapter context. Adapter checkpoint recovery is not validated.
+
+For the template, append the following overrides (the script's final overrides
+take precedence)::
+
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=64
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=64
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear
+    actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=True
+
+Historical rank/alpha64 LoRA used the complete 60-layer/128-expert model,
+training EP4/SP4 on four nodes and rollout TP32/EP1. Two updates on the same
+16 training/evaluation examples yielded training rewards 90/128 and 94/128;
+greedy same-set evaluation changed 10/16 to 15/16. DSpark was enabled there.
+Step3 stalled and checkpoint saving was disabled. It is not evidence of
+generalization or accelerator validation of the new implementation.

+
+import torch

+
+_TEXT_TARGETS = (
+    r"model\.language_model\.layers\.\d+\."
+    r"(self_attn\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj)|"
+    r"mlp\.(shared_experts\.)?(gate_up_proj|down_proj))"

+    "model.language_model.layers.*.mlp.experts.down_proj",
+]
+
+
+def configure_m3_lora(config):
+    """Make all-linear text-only, including experts; preserve explicit targets."""
+    changes = {}
+    if config.target_modules == "all-linear":
+        changes["target_modules"] = _TEXT_TARGETS
+        if not config.target_parameters:
+            changes["target_parameters"] = list(_EXPERT_TARGETS)
+    if changes.get("target_parameters", config.target_parameters) and config.moe_mode is None:
+        changes["moe_mode"] = "independent"
+    return config.replace(**changes)
+
+
+def prepare_m3_lora_dtypes(model):
+    """Before sharding, retain FP32 adapters/router and BF16 frozen matrices.
+
+    Construct the model in FP32 first so router and correction-bias precision is
+    retained. The companion VeOmni preserve_frozen_dtype option must also be set
+    to prevent build_parallelize_model from undoing this storage policy.
+    """
+    for name, parameter in model.named_parameters():
+        if not parameter.is_floating_point():
+            continue
+        keep_fp32 = parameter.requires_grad or name == "mlp.gate.weight" or name.endswith(".mlp.gate.weight")
+        parameter.data = parameter.data.to(torch.float32 if keep_fp32 else torch.bfloat16)
+    for name, buffer in model.named_buffers():
+        if name.endswith(".e_score_correction_bias") and buffer.is_floating_point():
+            buffer.data = buffer.data.float()
+
+
+def _merge_projection(base, a, b, scale):
+    """Merge dense, shared, or per-expert B@A with bounded FP32 row storage."""
+    if base.ndim not in (2, 3) or a.ndim != b.ndim or a.ndim not in (2, 3):
+        raise ValueError("Unsupported MiniMax LoRA projection layout")
+    if base.ndim == 2 and a.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError("Dense MiniMax projection requires 2D adapters")
+    if a.shape[-2] != b.shape[-1] or (b.shape[-2], a.shape[-1]) != tuple(base.shape[-2:]):
+        raise ValueError("MiniMax LoRA adapter and base shapes disagree")
+    if a.ndim == 3 and (a.shape[0] != base.shape[0] or b.shape[0] != base.shape[0]):
+        raise ValueError("MiniMax expert adapter count disagrees with local base")
+    result = base.clone()
+    if base.ndim == 2:
+        return torch.addmm(base.float(), b.float(), a.float(), alpha=scale).to(base.dtype)
+    for expert in range(base.shape[0]):
+        ae, be = (a[expert], b[expert]) if a.ndim == 3 else (a, b)
+        result[expert] = torch.addmm(base[expert].float(), be.float(), ae.float(), alpha=scale).to(base.dtype)
+    return result

+
+def merged_m3_lora_weights(model, device, parallel_state):
+    """Yield merged public weights; never merge into actor/optimizer parameters.
+
+    All training ranks must exhaust this iterator in identical order. FSDP
+    gathers a local expert stack and its adapters; the export helper streams
+    expert rows across EP ranks. This is full weight sync, not adapter-only sync.
+    """

+    from veomni.lora.layers import LoraLinear
+    from veomni.lora.moe_layers import is_lora_moe_experts
+

+        raise TypeError("Expected a VeOmni-native LoRA model")
+    spec = M3ExportSpec.from_config(model.config)
+    dense, expert_weights = {}, {}
+    for name, layer in model.named_modules():
+        if isinstance(layer, LoraLinear):
+            if layer.merged:
+                raise ValueError("MiniMax export requires unmerged training adapters")
+            dense[name] = layer
+        elif is_lora_moe_experts(layer):
+            for projection in ("gate_up_proj", "down_proj"):
+                expert_weights[f"{name}.{projection}"] = (layer, projection)
+
+    def full(tensor):
+        tensor = tensor.detach().to(device, non_blocking=True)

+

+            if any(part in {"lora_A", "lora_B", "lora_scaling"} for part in name.split(".")):

+            value = full(parameter)
+            stem = name.removesuffix(".base_layer.weight")
+            if stem in dense:
+                layer = dense[stem]
+                adapter = layer.active_adapter
+                value = _merge_projection(
+                    value,
+                    full(layer.lora_A[adapter].weight),
+                    full(layer.lora_B[adapter].weight),
+                    layer.scaling[adapter],
+                )
+                name = stem + ".weight"
+            elif stem in expert_weights:
+                layer, projection = expert_weights[stem]
+                if projection == "gate_up_proj":
+                    gate, up = value.chunk(2, dim=1)
+                    value = torch.cat(
+                        [
+                            _merge_projection(
+                                base,
+                                full(layer.get_lora_A_weight(logical)),
+                                full(layer.get_lora_B_weight(logical)),
+                                layer._lora_scale_value,
+                            )
+                            for logical, base in (("gate_proj", gate), ("up_proj", up))
+                        ],

+                    )
+                else:
+                    value = _merge_projection(
+                        value,
+                        full(layer.get_lora_A_weight("down_proj")),
+                        full(layer.get_lora_B_weight("down_proj")),
+                        layer._lora_scale_value,
+                    )
+                name = stem
+            # Frozen dense biases keep their value but lose the native wrapper prefix.
+            if name.endswith(".base_layer.bias"):
+                bias_stem = name.removesuffix(".base_layer.bias")
